proposals.prompt:
Agents in a supermarket gridworld must collect their required items and leave through the exit. Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)

Demonstration 1 (required items: eggs):
  0: {at(0,5)} E
  1: {at(1,5)} INTERACT
  2: {at(1,5)} N
  3: {at(1,4)} E
  4: {at(2,4)} E
  5: {at(3,4)} E
  6: {at(4,4)} E
  7: {at(5,4)} E
  8: {at(6,4)} INTERACT
  9: {at(6,4)} W
 10: {at(5,4)} W
 11: {at(4,4)} W
 12: {at(3,4)} W
 13: {at(2,4)} W
 14: {at(1,4)} W

 16: {at(0,3)} N
 17: {at(0,2)} N
 18: {at(0,1)} INTERACT
 19: {at(0,1)} S
 20: {at(0,2)} E
 21: {at(1,2)} E
 22: {at(2,2)} E
 23: {at(3,2)} E

 27: {at(7,2)} E
 28: {at(8,2)} S
 29: {at(8,3)} E
 30: {at(9,3)} S
 31: {at(9,4)} S
 32: {at(9,5)} EXIT
 33: {at(9,5)} <terminal>

Propose norms using ONLY the atoms listed above. Do NOT define any new state properties or events: "abstraction" must be {}.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: The agent is obliged to interact at cell (1,5) at some point during the trip.
The agent is obliged to interact at cell (0,1) before the trip ends.
After interacting at cell (6,4), the agent is obliged to later interact at cell (0,1).
After interacting at cell (0,1), the agent is obliged to exit from cell (9,5).
The agent is prohibited from moving east while at cell (6,4).
The agent is prohibited from moving south while at cell (6,4).
The agent is prohibited from occupying cells (7,4) or (8,4).
The agent is prohibited from moving east while at cell (1,5).

The demonstrations are now shown in a lower-level representation that exposes distinctions hidden before (newly available: cart_possession, cart_location, hand, actions_primitive). Identify the hidden distinctions and use them to define higher-level state properties and/or events (in "abstraction"), possibly hierarchically, and propose norms expressed over them. Norms may also use the primitive atoms directly.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: On entering the store, the shopper is obliged to take the waiting cart from the cart bay before proceeding with the shopping trip.
It is prohibited to enter the shopping aisles from the cart bay unless the shopper already has a cart.
Items should not be carried by hand; shoppers must avoid ever being in a hand-full state.
A shopper is prohibited from picking up shelf items unless they are currently holding or pushing a cart.
After taking any required item while using a cart, the shopper is obliged to return or park the cart at the service counter.
An unattended cart may only be stationed at an approved parking spot: the initial cart bay or the service counter.
Putting down a cart is prohibited anywhere except at the service counter cell.
The shopper may exit only after the cart has been left at the service counter and the shopper is no longer holding the cart.

attempts.prompt:
Agents in a supermarket gridworld must collect their required items and leave through the exit. Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)
- hasCart -- the agent is holding/pushing a shopping cart
- cartAt(x,y) -- the cart is parked (or stationed) at cell (x,y)
- handFull -- the agent carries an item by hand
- actions PICKUP_CART, LEAVE_CART (put the cart down on the current cell), PICKUP_ITEM (take an item from an adjacent shelf); each of these is also an INTERACT

parsed.text: On entering the store, the shopper is obliged to take the waiting cart from the cart bay before proceeding with the shopping trip.
It is prohibited to enter the shopping aisles from the cart bay unless the shopper already has a cart.
Items should not be carried by hand; shoppers must avoid ever being in a hand-full state.
A shopper is prohibited from picking up shelf items unless they are currently holding or pushing a cart.
After taking any required item while using a cart, the shopper is obliged to return or park the cart at the service counter.
An unattended cart may only be stationed at an approved parking spot: the initial cart bay or the service counter.
Putting down a cart is prohibited anywhere except at the service counter cell.
The shopper may exit only after the cart has been left at the service counter and the shopper is no longer holding the cart.

[g1_no_enter_without_cart] FORBIDDEN: (without_cart ∧ entering_aisles_from_bay)  where at_cart_bay := at(1,5); without_cart := ¬hasCart; entering_aisles_from_bay := (at_cart_bay ∧ (N ∨ E))
